page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-8 is a memory-optimized server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs, which map to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The processor includes an L3 cache of 32 MB, an L2 cache of 0.5 MB, and an L1d cache of 32 KB. It supports hardware-level features such as AVX, AES, VAES, SHA_NI, and BMI2. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

In benchmark evaluations, the c2d-highmem-8 demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% with a stress-ng single-core score of 2928.59. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 11730.12 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 6622.0, both falling within the average range. Memory bandwidth is stable, recording 553.05 GB/sec for small block cached reads and 62.15 GB/sec for large block uncached reads. Large block uncached write bandwidth is measured at 39.95 GB/sec.

The instance exhibits a performance tradeoff in complex computational tasks. While it handles small-model LLM inference adequately, with 135M model prompt processing at 607.92 tokens/sec, its performance drops to the bottom 25% for medium-model prompt processing at 18.65 tokens/sec. Given its high memory density and average multi-core processing capabilities, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel compute. It is suited for database operations, software compilation, static web serving, and memory-intensive general-purpose applications.
